Messages.Author: Pullen
Messages.Body:
Screw You!
Type: Action Modifier/Reaction/Combat
Cost 1:blood:
Draw a card, discard down to your hand size.

Though I really want to be able to say Screw You 5-6 times a game, I doubt that this example it the best of what I'm looking for, a disciplinless cycle card that isn't an action or master. Right now it's burn option cards, but that is a little off to me, any better ideas?

Messages.Author: Ashur
Messages.Body:
I am generally opposed to cards that affect your hand/library/ash heap without any real interaction with minions (except the cost, in this case).

"My strategy? Luck is my strategy, of course."

Messages.Body:

I think the game could do with more hand manipulation. Dreams and Barrens are highly-contested masters with good reason.

I would go more on the way of :

Emergency plan
Type : Action modifier
Cost : 1 blood
Play only if a reaction was played this action. Discard two cards. No more than one Emergency plan can be played per turn per methuselah.

A Black hand version may also be a good idea, since they are pretty good at planning it seem.

Messages.Author: Pullen
Messages.Body:
Scrounging
Type: Action
+1 stealth action.
Look at up to 3 cards from the top of your library and move up to 2 of them to your hand (shuffle and discard afterward).

This was the card that I was thinking of when I made this, now I do think my original is to good, maybe a once per turn clause, but the cards I have seen so far are weaker then Scrounging.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
I can't quite put my finger on what it is that bothers me, but it doesn't feel quite right for a disciplineless card. For something like this for the Black Hand, I could see it - Black Hand can do [whatever] and maybe a Seraph can do it slightly better (more cards, no cost, whatever).

As a disciplineless card, I don't know ... too much control for too little cost, or something. I'm not 100% sure what it is that doesn't quite gel for me.

Messages.Author: Miasmat
Messages.Body:
High Orun does something similar and is (sort of) disciplineless.

> High Orun
> Type:Action Modifier/Reaction
>
> Requires a Laibon with three or more Orun.
> For the remainder of this action, cards that require any Disciplines cost this Laibon 1 less blood, and your hand size is one card larger.
>
Sure, "a Laidon with three or more Orun" is a pretty different cost from "a vampire with capacity above 4", and the "cards that require any Disciplines cost this Laibon 1 less blood" is an extra bit of awesome, but the card flow effect is similar to your proposal and this card hasn't been mentioned yet.

Messages.Author: Pullen
Messages.Body: @Miasmat: Well personal I think the most of the 3 Orun/Aye cards are kind of janky, but I would also argue that plus hand is way better then draw a card and discard down, plus it's free, and the other affect, so I would put them on the same level, but the Liabon got hosed with the Orun/Aye cards, so I can't say thats a bad thing

I like the idea, but it's a very powerful affect, 3 cards would bring it down to a 4 card push, but then is it better then a Dreams as your taking a master slot now. It also lakes the interaction with minions that I was looking for in the first place. Most cards that enable card draw are master cards that sit their and I was looking for more mid action play that wasn't "Well let me tap this Dream's and Barrens and then see how my hand is."

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Pullen wrote:
> I like the idea, but it's a very powerful affect, 3 cards would bring it down to a 4 card push, but then is it better then a Dreams as your taking a master slot now. It also lakes the interaction with minions that I was looking for in the first place. Most cards that enable card draw are master cards that sit their and I was looking for more mid action play that wasn't "Well let me tap this Dream's and Barrens and then see how my hand is."
>
Yeah, 4 probably is over the top. I was running a couple of alternatives round in my head - "Choose cards after replacing", "Replace this card after you have performed these discards", "4 cards", "3 cards" etc. - and probably picked the least acceptable.

I think my issue with the minion card is that it's a little easy to use a) in your own turn (in at least some versions, anyway) and b) repeatedly. The M:OoT addresses both of those, without the need for a mountain of card text.

I'm pretty sure there's something in this sort of space - disciplineless discard - that would hit the mark, but I'm not sure what exactly.
